items.title: Bob Stewart interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006
items.q: I mean I started out with Arthur Blythe in his quartet, quintet.

ctx.x: “Mo Better Blues” right. And during the record date Milt Hinton was on the date. And I asked him, I said since you were there and I know you migrated to Chicago in the late teens when you were like ten or eleven years old, why did they stop using the tuba? And his answer, coming from a person who was not a tuba player, was, “Well you know the tuba was like a country instrument. It was an instrument for parades and stuff like that. And we were moving north. We were moving up to the city. And it just wasn’t hip…

drummer, a guitar player, who quite often had, by that time they were starting to be amplified, the guitar, there’s no way you could do that. I mean I started out with Arthur Blythe in his quartet, quintet. And I can’t tell you how many cuts I got trying to maintain that thing without an amplifier with a contemporary drummer. And still we weren’t playing as loud as one of those big bands. Trying to maintain a four feel and that contemporary style of playing, the bass function. And I mean swollen lips and ice…
